editorial.headline: Playgroup Education: Nationally Open, Not Blocked by Bali’s Moratorium
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers playgroup and preschool education for young children, including formal collaborations between recognised foreign and Indonesian educational institutions.
editorial.body:
Playgroup education is an early-childhood activity for children aged two to six, with particular priority given to ages three and four. Its scope includes playgroups run by government or the community, as well as preschool provision that combines educational and child-welfare programmes from birth to age six, prioritising children aged two to four. The category is therefore not merely a place for supervised activity: it describes a defined early-years educational setting.

The activity can be managed by government or by the community. It is open across Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar scales, giving the category a broad operating range rather than confining it to one size of provider. Its stated scope also includes playgroups created through cooperation with foreign educational institutions. Where that cooperation forms a formal educational pathway, the record describes a playgroup educational unit organised or managed through collaboration between an accredited or recognised foreign educational institution and an Indonesian educational institution.

Nationally, the investment position is clear. The activity is TERBUKA for PMA, with a national foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. In plain terms, foreign ownership may reach the full permitted ceiling nationally. The cited national basis is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. That openness sits alongside the activity’s educational character: the record frames the work around early-childhood education, community or government management, and—in the collaboration case—a structured relationship between foreign and Indonesian educational institutions.

Bali requires its own reading, but the outcome here is also direct. The provincial rule blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanently. This activity is not blocked by that moratorium. The record identifies its OSS risk at the Besar scale as Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, and marks the Bali position as OK_or_HIGHER_RISK. Accordingly, a PMA registration for this activity is not barred in Bali by the stated moratorium. The distinction matters: national openness is real, and the Bali rule does not reverse it for this activity on the facts provided.
